t: Count Good Integers on a Grid Path — Digit DP with a Monotone Constraint
o: Pad x to 16 digits, lay them in a 4×4 grid, and read the 7 cells hit by a fixed path given by directions. x is good iff those 7 digits are non-decreasing. Since the path only moves down/right, its cells appear in increasing row-major order, so a left-to-right digit DP that remembers the last path digit works. Count f(r) - f(l-1) with a tight-bound digit DP over 16 positions; l, r up to 9e15 fits exactly in 16 digits.
k: Path cells are visited in increasing row-major index order, so a positional digit DP can enforce non-decreasingness with a 'last path digit' state.
States: position (16) × tight (2) × last digit (11) — tiny; answer = f(r) - f(l-1).
Leading zeros are real digits here (padding is part of the definition), so no 'started' flag is needed.

a.i: For each x in [l, r], build the 16-digit string, walk the path, and check non-decreasing. Only usable for narrow ranges.
s: Precompute the 7 path cell indices from directions.
For each x, pad to 16 digits and extract path digits.
a.t: O((r - l + 1) · 7) — linear in range width

a.i: Count good 16-digit strings ≤ N with memoized DP over (position, tight, last path digit). Non-path cells are free; path cells must be ≥ the previous path digit. Answer = f(r) - f(l-1).
s: Convert directions into the ordered list of path indices; mark onpath[16].
dp(p, tight, last): try digits 0..hi; skip path digits below last; carry last forward only on path cells.
Memoize; evaluate for r and l-1 and subtract.
a.t: O(16 · 2 · 11 · 10) per evaluation — constant-size digit DP, called twice

w: Digit DP is the intended solution; the brute force validates it on small ranges. Pitfalls: remembering that leading zeros are genuine digits (padding is part of the specification, so no 'started' state), enforcing the constraint in path-visiting order (which equals index order here), and computing f(l-1) safely (l ≥ 1). Counts reach ~9e15, so use 64-bit / BigInt. Follow-up: what if directions could revisit cells or the path length varied?
